classification.difficultyReason: Express the height and parallel sides using trigonometry, then substitute into the trapezium area formula.

content.prompt:
A rain gutter is to be constructed from a sheet of metal of width 30 cm by bending up one third of the sheet on each side through an angle $\theta$.

Show that the cross-sectional area of the gutter is $A=100\sin\theta+100\sin\theta\cos\theta$.

spec.description: An open gutter cross-section with a horizontal base and equal sides rising outward. Reference lines extend horizontally outward from the bends. Three consecutive 10 cm dimension intervals show the original flat sheet. Curved arrows measure each bend from its outward horizontal reference.
spec.mathematics: The base and each folded side have length 10 cm. The gutter height is 10 sin theta and each side contributes horizontal projection 10 cos theta. The outside dimension intervals measure the original sheet sections, not the folded horizontal projections.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram content is permanently visible; no solution annotations are included.

answer.worked:
Each third of the sheet is $10$ cm wide.

Height of trapezium: $h=10\sin\theta$ cm.

Top parallel length: $a=10+20\cos\theta$ cm.

Bottom parallel length: $b=10$ cm.

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{h}{2}(a+b)\\A&=\frac{10\sin\theta}{2}\bigl(10+(10+20\cos\theta)\bigr)\\A&=5\sin\theta(20+20\cos\theta)\\A&=100\sin\theta+100\sin\theta\cos\theta\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
